Package com.egradx.notification.delivery

Class EgradxNotificationDispatcher

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.notification.delivery.EgradxNotificationDispatcher
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.context.Lifecycle, org.springframework.context.Phased, org.springframework.context.SmartLifecycle
public class EgradxNotificationDispatcher extends Object implements org.springframework.context.SmartLifecycle
Delivers what the outbox holds.

Each round: claim a batch of due deliveries in one short transaction, send them concurrently on virtual threads outside any transaction, then record each result in its own short transaction. Nothing holds a database connection or a row lock while waiting on a provider — the demo app's relay held both across its whole batch, which is fine for a local broker and not for an SMTP server that takes seconds to answer.

Safe to run on every instance at once: claiming uses FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, and a claimed row stays invisible to other dispatchers for the lease duration. An instance that dies mid-send loses nothing; the lease lapses and someone else retries. Delivery is therefore at-least-once, which is what EgradxNotificationChannel warns implementations about.

Runs on its own two threads rather than via @Scheduled. Using @Scheduled would have meant either sharing the application's scheduler — so a slow batch delays the application's own jobs, as the demo app's outbox relay delays its SSE heartbeat — or registering a TaskScheduler bean, which would make Spring Boot's own scheduler back off and quietly move every @Scheduled method in the application onto this library's threads. Neither is acceptable for a library; owning private threads is.

Each attempt is observed as egradx.notification.delivery (see begin(com.egradx.notification.delivery.EgradxNotificationDispatcher.ClaimedDelivery)); a delivery given up on counts towards egradx.notification.delivery.dead, and a result that arrived too late to be recorded towards egradx.notification.delivery.discarded.

    • onDeliveriesEnqueued

      @TransactionalEventListener(fallbackExecution=true) public void onDeliveriesEnqueued(EgradxDeliveriesEnqueuedEvent event)
      Delivers promptly after a submit commits instead of waiting for the next poll. Never fires for a rolled-back transaction, so a rolled-back message is never even looked for.

    • cleanup

      public int cleanup()
      Deletes SENT and DEAD deliveries past their retention, messages left with no deliveries, and in-app notifications past theirs. Runs on its own schedule; public so an operator can trigger it.

      In-app retention lives here only so that there is one maintenance job, not two; it touches nothing but in-app tables, and in-app publishing never involves this dispatcher.

      Returns:
      how many deliveries were deleted
